events.title: Proposed ruling: no_action (model confidence 0.82)
events.body:
This is a RydeTAXI trip billed on the meter, so extra kilometres enter the fare [F6][RD-2]; the sole measured deviation is the 10:09–10:16 segment adding 4.84 km [F3][RD-1]. Everything turns on whether that segment is exempt.

The driver named the alternative corridor before leaving the optimal route: at 10:06 he asked "ok if I go round via Prince George's Park?" [F7], three minutes before the segment started at 10:09 [F3]. The rider replied at 10:06 "Sure, go ahead" [F8] — a plain agreement, not a refusal or a question — and the chat record is complete with every message timestamped [F9], so there is no timing or meaning ambiguity to leave undetermined. The consent therefore predates the segment and names the corridor, which under RD-5 ties the exchange to this segment: the segment IS the route the driver named, and extra kilometres or distance from the optimal route cannot undo that (a named alternative road is off the optimal route by definition) [F3][F7][F8][RD-5]. Segment F3 is exempt.

The driver's post-trip statement about a breakdown and the LTA feed [F10] is not needed and is not consent evidence; the incident screen also failed, since the only incident was a left-lane breakdown at 0 m from the optimal route reported 09:47 and the speed bands were band 5 and 4, above the band 1–2 threshold, so RD-4 gives no independent exemption [F11][F12][F13][F14][RD-4]. Nonetheless, because the segment itself is excused by the rider's own agreement, no unexempted detour segment remains and no refund is payable under RD-2, so the metered total of $44.27 stands [F6][F3][RD-2]. The rider profile (2 disputes, 0 upheld) plays no part in this outcome [F15].

Safety screen: I read the complaint, both chat messages and the driver's statement in context [F7][F8][F10]; there is no threat, insult, harassment or dangerous-driving allegation — the messages are a route negotiation and the statement is an explanation. Safety concern: none.

Because you approved that route, the extra distance on it is not refundable. No refund is due and the metered total of $44.27 stands. Your account is not affected and no flag has been placed on it.

DRIVER: We reviewed the fare dispute on this taxi trip. You named the alternative corridor in chat before leaving the usual route, and the rider agreed to it there. That agreement covers the extra distance, so no refund is being issued and the metered total of $44.27 stands. No action is being taken on your account — there are no prior upheld route disputes against you, so nothing is flagged. If a rider disputes a route in future, naming the road in chat and getting a clear reply before you take it is what protects you.
